newsitem.title: USA: East, West Coast rappers pledge peace, promise tour.
newsitem.headline: East, West Coast rappers pledge peace, promise tour.

text.p: A contingent of rap artists from the East and West Coasts has pledged to end their feud and set tentative plans for a joint "hip hop peace tour" and album, a spokesman for the Nation of Islam said Friday.

The rappers, which included West Coast recording star Snoop Doggy Dogg and the East Coast representatives Chuck D and Doug E. Fresh, met in Chicago on Thursday under the auspices of Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan.
"This will bridge the divide," Nation of Islam spokesman Richard Muhammad told Reuters on Friday.

The assembly of rappers announced plans at a Thursday news conference to launch a cross-country concert tour and to collaborate on an album -- both dedicated to slain rap stars Tupac Shakur and Notorious B.I.G.

Brooklyn-born Notorious B.I.G., whose real name was Christopher Wallace and who was also known as Biggie Smalls, died in an unsolved drive-by shooting after a Los Angeles party on March 9. Rival Tupac Shakur was killed last year in Las Vegas in another unsolved shooting.

Part of the motivation behind the meeting at Farrakhan's Chicago restaurant were suspicions that their murders might have grown out of the long-standing rivalry between East and West Coast factions. Artists and their supporters have accused each other of stealing lyrics and copying rap styles.

Farrakhan said Shawn "Puffy" Combs, head of Notorious B.I.G.'s rap label Bad Boy Entertainment, could not attend but sent word that he would support the unity effort. Rappers Ice T and Ice Cube also sent messages of support.
Gangsta rapper Notorious B.I.G. currently holds the No. 1 position on the U.S. music charts with his posthumously released album, "Life After Death," according to his label.
